---
title: "Page chat"
---

`page_chat()` creates a full-window chat application with a persistent chat home,
optional navigation pages, page-aware sidebars, and an artifact region. Use it
when chat is the primary application surface. For an embedded chat in a larger
Shiny layout, continue to use [`chat_ui()`](api/chat_ui.qmd).

## Migrate an existing chat

For a Shiny Core app, replace the outer `ui.page_fillable()` and `chat_ui()`
combination with `page_chat()`. The server-side `Chat` instance keeps the same
ID and behavior.

```{.python file="app.py"}
# Before
from shiny import App, ui
from shinychat import Chat, chat_ui

app_ui = ui.page_fillable(chat_ui("chat"))

def server(input, output, session):
    chat = Chat("chat")

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

```{.python file="app.py"}
# After
from shiny import App
from shinychat import Chat, page_chat

app_ui = page_chat("Assistant", id="chat")

def server(input, output, session):
    chat = Chat("chat")

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

For Shiny Express, call `page_chat()` in place of `chat.ui()` and
`ui.page_opts(fillable=True)`. The helper configures the page itself.

```{.python file="app.py"}
# Before
from shiny.express import ui
from shinychat.express import Chat

chat = Chat("chat")
chat.ui()
ui.page_opts(title="Assistant", fillable=True)
```

```{.python file="app.py"}
# After
from shinychat.express import Chat, page_chat

chat = Chat("chat")
page_chat("Assistant", id="chat")
```

## Compose a page

The home page always contains the chat. Add secondary pages with
`chat_nav_panel()`, configure a home or page-specific sidebar with
`chat_sidebar()`, and use `chat_artifact()` for initial artifact content.
This complete Core app echoes submitted text and shows it in the artifact.

```{.python file="app.py"}
from shiny import App, reactive, ui
from shinychat import (
    Chat,
    chat_artifact,
    chat_nav_panel,
    chat_sidebar,
    page_chat,
)

app_ui = page_chat(
    "Research assistant",
    id="chat",
    toolbar=ui.input_action_button("clear_chat", "Clear conversation"),
    sidebar=chat_sidebar(
        ui.p("Recent conversations"),
        history=False,
        width=300,
    ),
    pages=[
        chat_nav_panel(
            "Sources",
            ui.p("Sources selected during this session appear here."),
            sidebar=True,
            toolbar=True,
        ),
        chat_nav_panel(
            "Settings",
            ui.input_switch("compact", "Compact answers"),
            sidebar=chat_sidebar(
                ui.p("Settings"),
                open="closed",
                width=260,
            ),
            toolbar=ui.input_action_button("save_settings", "Save settings"),
        ),
        chat_nav_panel(
            "About",
            ui.p("This app demonstrates page_chat()."),
            sidebar=False,
        ),
    ],
    artifact=chat_artifact(
        ui.p("Submit a question to inspect it here."),
        title="Latest request",
        width=400,
    ),
)


def server(input, output, session):
    chat = Chat("chat")

    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.clear_chat)
    async def _():
        await chat.clear_messages()

    @chat.on_user_submit
    async def _(user_input: str):
        await chat.append_message(f"You asked: {user_input}")
        await chat.artifact.show(
            ui.p(user_input),
            title="Latest request",
        )


app = App(app_ui, server)
```

`sidebar=True` supplies the default conversation-history sidebar when `Chat`
has a client and history enabled. Pass a
`chat_sidebar()` object when the page needs additional content or a different
initial width and open state. A navigation page can set `sidebar=False` to
remove it, use `sidebar=True` to use the default history sidebar, or supply
its own `chat_sidebar()`. `chat_ui_history("chat")` is available when an
advanced layout needs a history view bound to a specific chat ID outside a
`page_chat()` sidebar.

By default, a navigation page has no toolbar. Set `toolbar=True` to move the
same home toolbar into that page, preserving its input and output state. Supply
an HTML child for `toolbar` to use a page-specific toolbar instead. `None` is
not a toolbar value.

The artifact starts closed unless `chat_artifact(open=True)` is used. From the
server, `chat.artifact.show()`, `.update()`, `.hide()`, and `.toggle()` change
the artifact without replacing the chat. `show()` and `update()` accept
htmltools or Shiny UI content, including Shiny inputs and outputs.

The same composition helpers work with Shiny Express. Keep `page_chat()` as the
only top-level UI item and place application UI in its `toolbar`, `pages`,
sidebars, or artifact.

```{.python file="app.py"}
from shiny import reactive, ui
from shiny.express import input
from shinychat import chat_nav_panel, chat_sidebar
from shinychat.express import Chat, page_chat

chat = Chat("chat")

page_chat(
    "Research assistant",
    id="chat",
    toolbar=ui.input_action_button("clear_chat", "Clear conversation"),
    sidebar=chat_sidebar(history=False),
    pages=[
        chat_nav_panel(
            "About",
            ui.p("This page keeps the chat mounted."),
            sidebar=False,
            toolbar=True,
        ),
        chat_nav_panel(
            "Settings",
            ui.p("Settings"),
            toolbar=ui.input_action_button("save_settings", "Save settings"),
        )
    ],
)


@reactive.effect
@reactive.event(input.clear_chat)
async def _():
    await chat.clear_messages()
```

## Ownership and compatibility

`page_chat()` owns the page shell, full-height chat layout, chat history
placement, navigation controls, and responsive sidebar behavior. It fixes the
chat's `height`, `fill`, and `show_history` settings, so do not pass those
arguments through to `page_chat()`.

Do not wrap `page_chat()` in `ui.page_fillable()`, `ui.layout_sidebar()`, or a
raw `ui.sidebar()`. `chat_sidebar()` deliberately uses Shiny's sidebar
vocabulary but is a shinychat configuration object, not a `shiny.ui.Sidebar`.
This lets page chat manage one header toggle, mobile navigation, page-specific
sidebars, and a chat that remains mounted while users navigate.

In Express, `page_chat()` owns the complete top-level page composition. Extra
top-level UI, including a second chat root, is rejected. In Core, make
`page_chat()` the application's page UI and compose supporting UI through its
arguments. Existing `chat_ui()` applications remain supported and are the
right choice when chat is only one region of an application.

For signatures and all configuration options, see the
[Shiny Core reference](api/index.qmd#shiny-core) and
[Shiny Express `page_chat()` reference](api/express.page_chat.qmd).
